title: Add SDK parity conformance harness + fixtures (retries/timeouts/stream interruptions)
author: Mateusz Zielinski
release_notes: Go SDK: adds cross-language conformance tests for retry/backoff (429/5xx + Retry-After), network error classification, and streaming interruption error surfaces. No customer-facing API changes; test-only + internal harness.
description: Summary: This PR integrates the shared SDK parity conformance harness into redwood-sdk-go and adds the initial fixture set covering: (1) retryable HTTP responses (429/5xx) including Retry-After parsing, (2) network/transient transport failures, and (3) streaming interruptions (server FIN mid-event / partial chunk) with consistent typed error shape and request_id propagation. Motivation: During the SDK parity initiative, we’ve repeatedly found cross-language drift in edge-case behavior (esp. Retry-After handling and streaming disconnect surfacing). The goal of this harness is to make the Go SDK run the same behavioral tests as Python/TS so we can catch mismatches in CI before release. Scope/details: - Adds an internal conformance runner that spins up an httptest.Server and replays scripted responses from fixtures under testdata/conformance/fixtures/*.json. - Adds a deterministic fake clock + backoff recorder so tests assert retry timing windows (vs exact sleeps). - Adds fixtures for: * 429 with Retry-After (seconds) and Retry-After (HTTP-date) * 500/502/503 retry behavior (bounded attempts, jitter window) * transport errors (dial tcp refused, context deadline exceeded, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) classification as retryable vs terminal * streaming disconnects: mid-event EOF, truncated JSON payload, and proxy-like half-close behavior (client sees io.EOF while parsing SSE/data lines). - Plumbs request_id capture from response headers into the harness assertions (aligns with INT-1182 request_id visibility). What this PR does NOT do: - Does not change default retry/backoff settings (handled in PR #612) - Does not change public error types (handled in PR #624); this harness simply asserts current taxonomy stays aligned with the standard - Does not add any telemetry/logging (tracked separately in ENG-5129) Implementation notes: - The harness uses a Scenario file format shared across SDKs conceptually, but implemented in Go as a small parser over JSON fixtures with strict validation. - Streaming tests use chunked transfer encoding and a controllable writer that can: flush partial frames, close mid-write, and optionally omit the final '\n\n' SSE delimiter to simulate proxy truncation. - Retry tests do not sleep; they intercept the backoff function via an injected BackoffStrategy interface in internal/testutil and record requested delays; assertions check delay grows exponentially and stays within jitter bounds, and that Retry-After overrides computed backoff when present. CI: - Adds a new GitHub Actions job 'go-conformance' that runs 'go test ./... -run Conformance' on pull requests and main. - The job is marked required for merge (per ENG-5127). Testing: - go test ./... -run Conformance - go test ./... (full suite) - Validated locally that the 429 Retry-After (HTTP-date) fixture reproduces SUP-29477’s historical bug (previous code ignored date format; now asserted in tests; implementation already fixed in #612). Follow-ups: - Extend fixture coverage to include: 409 idempotency guidance (non-retryable), 408/499 semantics, and streaming cancellation (client-initiated) vs disconnect (server/proxy). - Once Python/TS runners are fully wired, we should align fixture names/IDs 1:1 and publish a small README in the shared conformance plan repo. Screenshots/logs: Example assertion output when Retry-After is not respected: "expected first retry delay to be derived from Retry-After=2s, got 400ms" (see ConformanceRetry429RetryAfterSeconds). Example assertion output when stream disconnect does not surface request_id: "expected error.request_id != ''" (see ConformanceStreamDisconnectMidEventEOF).
commits: test(conformance): add harness runner + scenario parser
test(conformance): add streaming interruption scenarios + helpers
ci: add go-conformance GitHub Actions job
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan (requested changes, 2026-02-12): "Nice. Two asks: (1) make sure we test Retry-After in both delta-seconds and HTTP-date formats; (2) avoid real time.Sleep in conformance tests so CI is stable." Mateusz Zielinski (reply): "Done. Added retry_429_retry_after_http_date.json and switched runner to inject FakeClock + BackoffRecorder; assertions now check computed delays without sleeping." Allison Grant (comment, 2026-02-13): "Can we assert jitter bounds instead of exact backoff? We should allow small variance across implementations." Mateusz Zielinski: "Yep; assertions now check delay within [base*(1-jitter), base*(1+jitter)] and only enforce monotonic growth + max cap." Sahana Iyer (comment, 2026-02-14): "CI: please split required job so conformance can be re-run quickly; also ensure it runs on forks without secrets." Mateusz Zielinski: "Updated workflow to add a dedicated go-conformance job with no secrets; uses standard go tooling only." Monica Patel (approval, 2026-02-18): "Ship it. This is exactly the gate we need before we flip defaults and message customers."
ci_summary: Initial run failed due to flaky timing assertion (used time.Sleep). Updated harness to record backoff requests (no sleeping). Final status: pass. Checks: lint-go (pass), unit-tests (pass), go-conformance (pass), govulncheck (pass).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien after approvals from Ibrahim Khan and Monica Patel.
